analysis.title: Government formation talks continue in Sweden
key_insights: US 10-year Treasury yield reversed more than half of its October decline after a strong US labour market report, slightly higher US inflation and hawkish Fed comments. European yields followed, led by France. Expectations of further Fed and ECB rate hikes increased.

SEB views continued central bank rate hikes from levels that already look unsustainable given high public debt as a risky gamble. It expects higher rates to hit US households and the weak housing market, with negligible impact on the AI investments driving US growth.
SEB sees it as worrying for longer-term stability that parts of the Fed, historically forward-looking and focused on downside growth risks, now scrutinise tenths of a percentage point in inflation.
US equities recovered much of a sharp Friday-evening decline, with the S&P 500 closing 0.4% lower. Nvidia fell almost 5% at one point and closed down 2%, and is down 33% from its early-October peak.
The Financial Times reports efforts to persuade Nvidia's board to reinstate the recently ousted Jensen Huang as CEO.
Asian equities are mostly lower, with the largest declines in Korea and Taiwan. US equity futures point to losses of a few tenths of a percent and European futures are unchanged.

Week ahead: the minutes of the Fed's late-October meeting (rates held, two dissenting votes) are a data highlight. The Trump, Xi and Putin summit at APEC in China is expected to draw more attention, with a nuclear agreement the main purpose and the Iran and Ukraine wars and trade policy likely on the agenda.
Anthropic's IPO, expected to be one of the largest ever, is planned to price on Wednesday with trading starting Thursday.

Swedish labour market data (LFS) is due Friday. SEB says the LFS is too volatile for firm conclusions from single months and maintains that the Riksbank is too optimistic about the labour market, citing alternative employment measures and indicators.

Sweden government formation: the Centre Party backs Magdalena Andersson's plan for a Social Democrat, Centre and Green government negotiating policy with the Left Party, on a roughly 100-point proposal. The Left Party insists on joining the government, so the coalition still lacks parliamentary support.

Ulf Kristersson reports his exploratory talks to the Speaker tomorrow and SEB expects him to acknowledge insufficient support for a centre-right government. The Speaker will probably move toward a third parliamentary vote on a prime minister, but another Andersson vote would only confirm no progress and Kristersson has no prospect of winning one.

Andersson argues in an opinion article that a Moderate and Social Democrat government is the only solution if her proposed coalition fails. The Moderates have rejected this at least with Andersson as prime minister. Two PM votes remain and speculation is growing that a snap election will be hard to avoid.

Norway's Q4 Inflation Expectations Survey (Thursday) is important, especially business leaders' expectations, which lead domestic inflation. The Committee has flagged elevated expectations as a risk of entrenched inflation. Social partners' wage growth estimates are also watched.
